themes_detail.label: Street damage spike post-winter
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints surged to 201 THIS WEEK, up 253% from the 8-week baseline of 56.9 per week (z-score: 7.39), suggesting winter weather has accelerated pothole and pavement deterioration across Tottenville/Great Kills at a rate the city may struggle to address.
evidence: 201 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 56.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (253% spike, z-score: 7.39)
Street reconstruction is a repeated, unfunded Community Board budget request, indicating chronic underinvestment
Spike follows major snow/ice event 3 weeks ago (2633 complaints vs. 211.8 avg), suggesting freeze-thaw cycle damage
reporting_angles: Interview DOT on repair timeline and whether winter damage budget exists for this district
Canvass residents on specific problem intersections and safety concerns from deteriorated roads

themes_detail.label: Tree damage and overgrowth surge
themes_detail.summary: Damaged tree complaints reached 35 THIS WEEK (294% above the 8.9 weekly baseline, z-score: 5.52) and overgrown tree/branch complaints hit 19 (375% above 4.0 baseline, z-score: 5.3), suggesting winter storm damage and deferred maintenance on the street tree canopy.
evidence: 35 damaged tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 8.9 weekly average (294% spike, z-score: 5.52)
19 overgrown tree/branch complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.0 weekly average (375% spike, z-score: 5.3)
Forestry services and street tree maintenance is a repeated, unfunded Community Board budget request
reporting_angles: Investigate Parks Dept staffing and budget for emergency tree removal in this district
Document specific safety hazards from fallen branches or weakened trees affecting homes and roads

themes_detail.label: Illegal posting vandalism wave
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints hit 35 TWO WEEKS AGO, up 900% from the 3.5 weekly baseline (z-score: 11.32), suggesting a coordinated or sustained tagging/graffiti campaign or lapse in enforcement and removal across the district.
evidence: 35 illegal posting complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 3.5 weekly average (900% spike, z-score: 11.32)
Increase in enforcement of illegal dumping laws is a repeated Community Board budget request
No follow-up data this week; unclear if spike has subsided or persists
reporting_angles: Check with NYPD and Sanitation Dept on whether a specific posting ring was identified and actions taken
Survey residents and business owners on whether tagging persists and impact on neighborhood perception

themes_detail.label: Noise complaints from houses of worship
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints from houses of worship reached 5 THIS WEEK, a 3900% spike from the 0.1 weekly baseline (z-score: 14.74), suggesting a localized, acute issue affecting a specific congregation or event rather than a pattern.
evidence: 5 noise complaints from houses of worship THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average (3900% spike, z-score: 14.74)
Spike is highly localized and sudden; suggests specific event, service, or equipment issue rather than trend
No prior context in community board or constituent data
reporting_angles: Identify which house(s) of worship are involved and whether a specific event or sound issue triggered complaints
Interview neighbors and the congregation to understand complaint nature and whether mediation is needed

themes_detail.label: Wood pile abandonment issue
themes_detail.summary: Wood pile remaining complaints hit 6 LAST WEEK, a 4700% spike from the 0.1 weekly baseline (z-score: 17.76), pointing to either a single large illegal dumping incident or a coordinated disposal problem in an industrial or waterfront area.
evidence: 6 wood pile remaining complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average (4700% spike, z-score: 17.76)
Increase in enforcement of illegal dumping laws is a repeated Community Board budget request
Tottenville/Great Kills has industrial and waterfront zones susceptible to bulk waste dumping
reporting_angles: Locate the specific site(s) with wood pile complaints and determine source (construction debris, salvage operation, illegal dump)
Assess whether Sanitation Dept enforcement is adequate and whether illegal dumping is recurrent in waterfront/industrial areas
